title: American Gangster film based on true story that's a 'must watch' if you love the Godfather - NewsBreak
text: The biographical crime film, Kill the Irishman, is creating quite a buzz among viewers . The movie, which can be streamed on Amazon Prime and Apple TV , is based on Rick Porrello's book To Kill the Irishman: The War That Crippled the Mafia, and tells the story of Irish-American gangster Danny Greene. According to the official synopsis: "Kill the Irishman chronicles the true story of Danny Greene, a tough union rep who climbed the ranks of Cleveland's underworld to become a formidable adversary, eventually sparking a turf war with the Italian Mafia. The film focuses on Greene's ascent to power and his subsequent assassination. "Kill the Irishman delves into Greene's ambition, his confrontations with the Mafia, and the repercussions of his actions on organized crime in Cleveland and beyond." READ MORE: Fresh health fears sparked as Donald Trump's 'hidden leg brace' spotted READ MORE: Melania Trump grins and bears as Donald describes painful humiliation in four words Directed by Jonathan Hensleigh, the film boasts a star-studded cast including Ray Stevenson, Vincent D'Onofrio, Val Kilmer, Christopher Walken, Linda Cardellini, Tony Darrow, and Robert Davi, among others. Also available on Apple TV, the film has been lauded by fans of gangster movies, with some even calling it a 'must watch' for those who love films like The Godfather, according to the Express. One critic shared in an IMDb review: "Great cast, great acting, and an absolute must-see for mafia-philes. "Unlike many bio-dramas, this one moves along at a rocket pace, leaving the audience on the edge of their seats." Another praised the film as "very underrated." Upon its debut, Kill the Irishman garnered a mixed bag of critiques and drew comparisons to Martin Scorsese's iconic Goodfellas from 1990. The flick snagged a contentious 63% rating from Rotten Tomatoes critics, who remarked: "Kill the Irishman may not add much in the way of new ingredients to its crowded genre, but the admirable efforts of a solidly assembled cast add extra depth to a familiar story." Yet, some reviewers were quick to defend the movie, with one asserting it's "the best true crime drama out there" and another concurring they "absolutely love this [film]." Kill the Irishman isn't the only mobster movie getting buzz on Amazon; another crime flick, hailed as 'poetic,' has made a comeback. Featuring two overlooked Tinseltown icons, the 90s gangster epic, Miller's Crossing, crafted by Joel and Ethan Coen, is now being lauded as "an all time classic" by fans. This cinematic gem weaves the tale of dueling mobs during the 1929 Prohibition era, with Irish kingpin Leo O'Bannon, played by Albert Finney, igniting a turf war as he shields his lady's brother, Bernie, who finds himself in hot water with a rival faction. Little does he know, his main squeeze is secretly entangled with his right-hand man, Tom Reagan, portrayed by Gabriel Byrne. The flick scores an almost 'perfect' mark, with one Rotten Tomatoes user gushing: "All-time classic. This has all the hallmarks of a noir. "The script is very complicated but never convoluted to the point where you can't follow it, which is a testament to the masterful editing. My only real complaint is while the music is good, I wish it was used a bit more, but this really is never dry. Everyone should give this a try once."
